punchline: The castaways passed over the nearest islands because of what they assumed about them, not what they knew.
thirty_sec: Twenty men from the sunk whaleship Essex had three open boats and no charts. Owen Chase writes that the council knew nothing of the Society Islands and feared whoever might live there, so they set out for the South American coast instead. Thomas Nickerson, writing decades later, says the captain had wanted the islands and that they were ten days away at most. The decision rested on a gap in knowledge.
